edges.description: Neoplastic neuroblasts mature into ganglion cells. In nodular tumors, ganglion cells carry the MYCN gain found in the neuroblasts, while Schwann cells do not.

In co-culture, neuroblastoma tumors and cell lines stimulate Schwann cell proliferation, which the authors read as a hint that neoplastic neuroblasts drive stromal growth in tumors. The evidence is in vitro and says nothing about where the stromal cells come from.
In 7 of 8 nodular tumors studied, the neuroblasts of the nodule carried MYCN copy gain, consistent with the nodule being formed by the neoplastic neuroblast population.
The primary tumor forms a mass at its site of origin.
The primary tumor forms a mass at its site of origin.
Orphanet ties the clinical features of ganglioneuroblastoma, congenital Horner syndrome among them, to the location of the tumor. How the tumor produces the sign is not described.
Soluble Schwann cell products induce neuronal differentiation of neuroblastoma cells. The evidence is from cultured neuroblastoma cells, not from ganglioneuroblastoma tissue.
In the unfavorable subset, distant metastasis from the neuroblastomatous nodule is often already present at diagnosis, even when the primary tumor is completely resected.

nodes.description: A primary tumor of the adrenal medulla or extra-adrenal retroperitoneum forms an abdominal mass. In one referral series of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma, 74% of primary tumors were abdominal.

evidence.snippet: usually occurring in the posterior mediastinum, adrenal medulla and extra-adrenal retroperitoneum (but sometimes in the neck and pelvis)

evidence.reference_title: Ganglioneuroblastoma intermixed: Clinicopathological implications of diagnosis at presentation and genomic correlations.
evidence.snippet: The primary tumor was abdominal in 39 (74%) and thoracic in 14 patients (26%).

nodes.description: Congenital Horner syndrome is one of the clinical features of ganglioneuroblastoma that depend on where the tumor lies. The cited source gives no frequency.

evidence.snippet: characterized clinically by pain, stridor, shortness of breath, peripheral neurological signs, superior vena cava syndrome and congenital Horner syndrome, depending on the location of the tumor

nodes.description: Nearly half of patients with nodular ganglioneuroblastoma have stage 4 disease at diagnosis: 107 of 232 in an INRG analysis, in which overall survival for stage 4 was 35%. In a CCG/COG series, 53% of patients with the unfavorable subset had distant metastasis at diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Characteristics and outcome of patients with ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular subtype: a report from the INRG project.
evidence.snippet: Amongst 4071 patients in the INRG database with known INPC histological category, 232 patients with GNBn were identified. ... A cohort with superior outcome was identified: OS for GNBn patients younger than 18 months was 95%±5% (n=39) and for GNBn patients with stage 1, 2, 3, 4s was 95%±3% (n=125). Conversely, a poor outcome sub-group could also be identified: OS for stage 4 was 35%±7% (n=107).

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological characteristics of ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma: a report from the CCG and COG.
evidence.snippet: The UH group included ganglioneuroblastoma-nodular, unfavorable subset (GNB-N-US) tumors. Patients with the UH tumors had a high incidence (53%) of distant metastasis at the time of diagnosis

nodes.description: The malignant neuroblastic cells of the tumor, which form the microscopic neuroblastic nests of intermixed tumors and the nodules of nodular tumors. In a 1996 series of 20 maturing and mature neuroblastomas, the neuroblastic and ganglionic cells carried numerical chromosome aberrations, with near-triploidy in 18 of 19 tumors. Flow cytometry nonetheless reads most GN-maturing and intermixed tumors as diploid (160 of 191 in a CCG/COG series), which the authors suggest may reflect the predominance of Schwannian stromal cells in the samples.

evidence.reference_title: Role of ploidy, chromosome 1p, and Schwann cells in the maturation of neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Neuroblastic and ganglionic cells showed aberrations in the number of chromosomes. In situ hybridization and flow cytometry demonstrated near-trip-loidy in 18 of 19 tumors and pentaploidy in the remaining tumor.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological characteristics of ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma: a report from the CCG and COG.
evidence.snippet: In our series, the majority of GN-M and GNB-I tumors, even though they were biologically favorable with an excellent prognosis, had a diploid pattern determined by flow cytometry. This could be attributable to the fact that those tumors were mainly or predominantly composed of Schwannian stromal cells, and neuroblastic cells were not the main source of cells to be tested.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological characteristics of ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma: a report from the CCG and COG.
evidence.snippet: The majority (160/191, 84%) of GN-M and GNB-I tumors had a diploid pattern determined by flow cytometry.

nodes.description: Neoplastic neuroblasts differentiate into ganglion cells. Biologically favorable peripheral neuroblastic tumors are considered to mature by age-dependent steps from neuroblastoma through intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma to ganglioneuroma.

biological_processes: maturation of neuroblasts into ganglion cells

evidence.snippet: To note, tumors in the biologically favorable pNTs are considered to proceed by age-dependent differentiation/maturational steps from NB to GNB-i, and finally to GN.

nodes.description: The posterior mediastinum is one of the usual primary sites of ganglioneuroblastoma. In one referral series of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma, 26% of primary tumors were thoracic.

nodes.description: One or more macroscopic, usually hemorrhagic, Schwannian stroma-poor nodules of neuroblastoma within intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma tissue. The nodular components are not always aggressive, and the age-linked histopathology of the nodules predicts prognosis. Whether the nodule is a clone distinct from the rest of the tumor is contested (discussion gnb_nodule_clonality).

evidence.reference_title: Histopathology defines prognostic subsets of ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular.
evidence.snippet: The current study demonstrates that the nodular components in GNBn tumors are not always aggressive. The prognosis of these patients can be determined by the analysis of age-linked histopathologic features.

nodes.description: The Schwann-cell stroma that makes up more than half of an intermixed tumor and forms the background of a nodular one. The INPC names each category by its Schwannian stromal development, which gives intermixed tumors their elastic, yellowish-white gross appearance. In culture, neuroblastoma tumors and cell lines stimulate Schwann cell proliferation, and Schwann cell products induce neuronal differentiation of neuroblastoma cells. Whether the stromal cells are non-neoplastic cells recruited by the tumor or derive from the neoplastic clone is contested (discussion gnb_schwannian_stroma_origin).

evidence.snippet: Tumors in this category are elastic in consistency and yellowish white in color due to Schwannian stromal development (Fig. 2A).

INPC defines 4 categories in the pNTs: Neuroblastoma (NB; Schwannian stroma-poor), Ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed (GNB-i; Schwannian stroma-rich), Ganglioneuroma (GN; Schwannian stroma-dominant), and Ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular (GNB-n; composite, Schwannian stroma-rich/stroma-dominant and stroma-poor) ... In order to clarify their histologic characteristics, each category is often followed by its unique feature of Schwannian stromal development in parenthesis.

nodes.description: In localized intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma, studied together with ganglioneuroma, chemotherapy seemed not to be effective and incomplete resection leaving only minor residuals (under 2 cm) appeared sufficient. In nodular ganglioneuroblastoma of the unfavorable subset, a CCG/COG series found no significant survival difference between complete primary tumor resection (at least 95% removed before chemotherapy or irradiation) and biopsy or partial resection, in patients with or without distant metastasis. The non-significant differences favored complete resection, the non-stage 4 comparison included few incompletely resected patients, and prognosis depended significantly on stage.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment and outcome of Ganglioneuroma and Ganglioneuroblastoma intermixed.
evidence.snippet: Outcome was excellent and chemotherapy seems not effective while incomplete resection with minor residuals (<2 cm) appears to be sufficient for treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Is There a Role for Chemotherapy in Unresectable Ganglioneuroblastoma Intermixed?: A Case Series Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Four patients received chemotherapy but showed no significant tumor reduction postchemotherapy, and all required surgery afterward.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological characteristics of ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma: a report from the CCG and COG.
evidence.snippet: Complete primary tumor resection was not beneficial to those GNB-N-US patients, regardless of whether metastasis was present or not.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological characteristics of ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma: a report from the CCG and COG.
evidence.snippet: Complete resection: Complete or gross (≥95% of volume) tumor resection was achieved by single or multiple surgeries from the primary site before starting chemotherapy/irradiation therapy. ... the prognosis of patients with GNB-N-US was significantly dependent on clinical stage. ... For non-stage 4 patients, there was no significant difference in survival between patients with complete primary resection (85 cases) and with incomplete primary resection (16 cases), with 5-year EFS of 83.4% ± 9.1% vs. 60.6% ± 26.9% (p = 0.2227) and OS of 90.5% ± 7.2% vs. 80.0% ± 25.3% (p = 0.7176) ... The 5-year EFS for stage 4 patients with completely (74 cases) and incompletely resected (51 cases) primary tumors, respectively, was 24.3% ± 9.5% vs. 5.4% ± 5.2% (p = 0.1068) and OS was 38.5% ± 9.6% vs. 28.2% ± 11.9% (p = 0.5797)
